tob-10495: The middle canticle of Dante’s great poem follows the poet and his guide Virgil up the mountain of Purgatory, where souls climb terrace by terrace, purging the seven deadly sins. Here Dante meets old friends and enemies, learning that suffering willingly borne leads to Paradise. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow’s translation made this journey English readers’ own.
tob-10795: Monier-Williams, Oxford’s great Sanskrit scholar, examines how Buddhism grew out of — and reacted against — the Brahmanical religion of ancient India. He compares the Buddha’s teachings with the Vedas and Upanishads, tracing what the new faith kept and what it rejected. The book offers a Victorian scholar’s systematic view of India’s religious transformation.
tob-0095: This 1619 news-sheet tells the grim tale of the Flower sisters — charged with bewitching the Earl of Rutland’s house at Belvoir. Their confessions, wrung out under duress, led to the gallows-tree. The tract is a chilling firsthand record of an English witch trial.
tob-4295: Arthur Avalon’s Tantra Grounds — the Tantratattva — first bore Hindu Tantra westward, Englished with gloss by John Woodroffe. The work opened Shakti-worship’s thought to our readers. Woodroffe’s toil lit the lamp for all later western Tantra-study. It stays the classic English door to Tantra.
tob-10395: Waite’s Book of Ceremonial Magic is the great English study of ritual magic — its grimoires, rites, and history weighed with scholarly care. He separates genuine tradition from charlatanry with a sharp eye. The book remains the classic reference on the ceremonial art.
cia-0000124295: A November 1957 report on British-manufactured batteries possibly used in Sputniks I and II. If Western components flew in Soviet satellites, it raised sharp questions about export controls. The document follows the supply chain into orbit — trade policy, launched skyward.
cia-0000132595: An August 1960 report titled Cuba-Communist China. The Havana-Beijing axis was strengthening alongside the Moscow tie. The document is the triangle, forming: the island, between two giants.
cia-0000135895: A 1954 record of a weekly PBSUCCESS meeting with a deleted participant. The operation met weekly, like clockwork. The entry is the routine: the meeting, held — the attendee, unnamed.
cia-0000136095: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN authorizing continued flights into Toncontin. The Honduran airfield stayed busy. The document is the authorization: the flights, continued.
cia-0000136195: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for WELLBANKS reporting that a deleted person was being held — the truncated title cuts off where. The prisoner, noted — the identity, hidden. The entry is the detention: the holding, reported.
cia-0000136395: A 1953 cable on briefing P/A on the project. The personal assistant, briefed. The document is the briefing: the aide, informed.
cia-0000136995: A 1954 cable on lessons and themes to be pushed long term. The narrative, institutionalized. The document is the doctrine: the themes, embedded.
cia-0000140395: A 1952 file titled Research Projects. The projects, listed. The document is the program: the research, catalogued.
un-ga-res-195: Resolution 195 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1948. The third session's work. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-395: Security Council Resolution 395, cataloged with the year 1949 — the numbering suggests 1976, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1595: Security Council Resolution 1595, adopted in April 2005 — the Hariri resolution, creating an international commission to investigate the assassination of Lebanese prime minister Rafik Hariri. The Beirut bombing demanded answers. The resolution is the investigation: the murder, probed.
un-sc-res-1795: Security Council Resolution 1795, adopted in 2008 — aligned. The new year's Council deciding. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1895: Security Council Resolution 1895, cataloged with the year 2003 — the numbering suggests 2009, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000135695: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135695. The fateful papers, preserved. The entry is the preservation: the brigade, remembered — in Spanish.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d95: The Acting Secretary of State Stettinius to the adviser on political relations — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 95. The stand-in secretary's internal paper. The memo is the internal: Stettinius, directing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d195: A memorandum by Generalissimo Chiang's chief of staff, Stilwell — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 195. Vinegar Joe's paper on China. The memo is the general's: Stilwell, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d295: The Secretary of State to the President, November 23, 1943 — Document 295. A second that day. The memo is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d395: The Joint Chiefs of Staff to the President, November 30, 1943 — Document 395. The war's planners wrote the White House. The memo is the planners': the chiefs, briefing.
reflections-and-comments-1865-1895: Edwin Lawrence Godkin, the great editor of The Nation, reflects on thirty years of American life — politics, society, and morals. His high-minded, often sharp comments shaped liberal thought. The essential Godkin, in his own words. Reconstruction, reform, and the Gilded Age all feel his searching criticism.
arxiv-2605-08795: When a molecule lands on an insulator only a few atoms thick, its electrical energy levels shift in ways that decide how the whole device behaves. Kevin Lizárraga and four coauthors attack the problem from first principles, using ab initio quantum calculations to predict both the energy alignment and the charge state of such adsorbates. The 2026 paper serves nanoelectronics and surface science with parameter-free theory.
arxiv-2605-08895: Mapping hydrogen across the cosmos through its faint radio glow — intensity mapping — is plagued by earthly interference and instrument quirks. Pauline Gorbatchev, Jean-Luc Starck, Stefano Camera, and colleagues look beyond the standard power spectrum to sniff out those systematics in hydrogen intensity maps. The 2026 paper is cosmology: cleaning the cosmic signal.
arxiv-2605-08995: Clustering high-dimensional data — gene readings, images — strains classic methods. Long Feng and Dan Zhuang propose semiparametric elliptical mixture clustering, blending flexible modeling with the structure of elliptical distributions. The 2026 paper is practical statistics for the modern high-dimensional world.
arxiv-2605-09195: Language models forget over time — knowledge drifts — but the drift may have its own geometry. Rania Elbadry, Ahmed Heakl, Fan Zhang, and colleagues treat temporal knowledge drift as an independent axis in LLM representations. The 2026 paper maps forgetting as a direction in the model's inner space.
arxiv-2605-09295: Turning English questions into SQL is easier if the model first sketches the query's skeleton. Zhao Tan, Xiping Liu, Qing Shu, and colleagues predict that skeleton with LEAF-SQL: level-wise exploration with adaptive fine-graining. The 2026 paper is text-to-SQL with a plan-first strategy.
arxiv-2605-09595: Four-legged robots scrambling over rocky ground need control that is both fast and frugal — classic neuromorphic hardware territory. Zhuangyu Han and Abhronil Sengupta bring neuromorphic reinforcement learning to quadruped locomotion on uneven terrain. The 2026 paper is brain-inspired robotics for rough country.
arxiv-2605-09795: Hope speech — text that inspires, reassures, and uplifts — deserves detection in Dravidian languages too. Andrew Li and Sidney Wong show organic domain adaptation improves multi-class hope speech detection. The 2026 paper is NLP for under-served languages and kinder internet.
arxiv-2605-09995: Post-training mode collapse — models losing their diversity after fine-tuning — can be mitigated with annotations. This 2026 paper shows how careful annotation preserves variety. It is LLM training that keeps the model's full range. Diversity survives post-training fully intact.
plos-pone-0003395: Genetic counselors' future toolkit got a stress test in this 2008 paper. Using whole-genome data to predict a person's disease risk works for simple inherited disorders, but most diseases are not simple. The authors tested how accurately genome-wide prediction performs across trickier conditions, weighing its promise as a public-health tool against the real limits of the math.
plos-pone-0003495: Sequencing scientists invented a prep trick called the Long March in this 2008 methods paper. Short-read sequencers produce mountains of tiny fragments that are hard to stitch into long contigs, but this sample-preparation technique extended both contig length and coverage. The method helps high-throughput sequencing deliver more complete genomes from fragmented data.
plos-pone-0003595: Forensic scientists Marrone and Ballantyne profiled a DNA-chewing enzyme in this 2008 paper. BAL 31 nuclease from a marine bacterium digests single-stranded DNA, and synthetic test pieces revealed its sequence preferences. Knowing exactly where the enzyme cuts matters for both genome mapping and the forensic lab's molecular toolbox.
plos-pone-0003695: In 2008, Boukovinas, Papadaki, and Mendez tied tumor gene levels to chemo results. In patients getting gemcitabine plus docetaxel, the expression of BRCA1, RRM1, and RRM2 in tumors predicted who responded. The three-gene readout offers a step toward matching chemo to the tumor's own profile.
plos-pone-0003795: Sakai and Fukai asked when greed follows a famous law in this 2008 theory paper. Their analysis of reward maximization versus the matching law probes which strategies animals use when choosing. The math clarifies when maximizing payoffs naturally produces the matching pattern psychologists observe.
plos-pone-0003895: Working in 2008, a team showed cells tagging each other from the outside. Ecto-phosphorylation of the CD98 protein regulated how cells grip one another. The outside-in signaling reveals a fast lane for tuning cell-cell contact.
plos-pone-0003995: In 2008, van der Linden, Murre, and van Turennout watched categories form in the brain. Brain scans showed the ventral visual stream learning new object categories through experience. Birds of a feather truly flocked together in the mind's sorting office. The study proves the brain's visual categories are built by experience, not born.
plos-pone-0004095: In 2009, Shaish and Rinkevich asked if corals grow like trees. They tested whether branch polarity and tip dominance rule colony shape in a branching coral. Tree-like rules partly held in the sea animal. The study bridges plant botany and reef biology.
plos-pone-0004195: In 2009, Cameron and Dalerum counted billionaires' babies and grandbabies. Male-biased sex ratios among billionaires fit the famed Trivers-Willard effect. Rich mothers bore more sons, just as the old theory predicts. The neat finding extends the effect to modern humans today.
plos-pone-0004295: In 2009, Liang, Yang, and Pan pushed ovaries toward overgrowth. Activated PIK3CA in ovarian surface epithelium caused hyperplasia but no tumors. The cancer gene's push stalled before malignancy. The model separates growth from cancer. The result refines PIK3CA's role in ovarian cancer.
plos-pone-0355395: When someone taps your hand, can you tell how they see it from their side? This study tested spatial perspective-taking with ambiguous touch stimuli in children with autism or developmental coordination disorder. The results reveal how these children interpret touch differently — a window onto how their brains map the body in space.
plos-pone-0358595: Military families move constantly, and raising a neurodivergent child on that treadmill is brutally hard. This qualitative study followed British Armed Forces families navigating fragmented, contingent support services. Their stories expose the gaps — and show what steady, reliable help would actually look like.
plos-pone-0357395: Cold pain starts in sensory neurons — and the Nav1.8 sodium channel helps run the signal. This study showed Nav1.8 regulates calcium dynamics in the dorsal root ganglion under cold pain stimuli. Pinpointing the channel’s role in cold nociception makes it a concrete target for taming cold-triggered pain with future drugs.
plos-pone-0358195: Nuclear waste needs a tomb that lasts millennia. This paper studied the structure and leaching of basaltic glass-ceramics designed to immobilize simulated actinides — lanthanum, cerium, and neodymium standing in for the real thing. The leaching tests measure whether the waste stays locked inside the glass.
plos-pone-0357295: Tiny RNA molecules circulating in blood may track how well the aging brain thinks. This pilot study linked individual circulating microRNAs to continuous cognitive performance in a mixed inpatient-outpatient geriatric cohort. The RNA signatures could one day become simple blood tests for cognitive decline.
plos-pone-0356695: Work-life balance means something different inside Japan’s famously intense work culture. This paper developed the Japanese version of the work-life integration scale, focused specifically on the work environment in Japan. The validated tool lets researchers measure what Japanese workers actually experience — not what Western scales assume.
plos-pone-0357595: A fungus dwelling in tree bark manufactures antioxidant chemicals. This paper profiled the metabolites of Neopestalotiopsis clavispora — isolated from Oroxylum indicum stem bark — with UPLC-MS and tested their antioxidant efficacy. The fungal chemistry could yield new natural antioxidants for medicine and food.
plos-pone-0357795: Complex-valued neural networks promise richer computation — but they need rigorous stability guarantees. This paper developed sampled-data exponential stabilization for delayed complex-valued neural networks with quantized intermittent communication. The mathematics keeps these exotic networks stable under realistic, imperfect conditions.
plos-pone-0357495: ANCA antibody tests guide vasculitis diagnosis — but testing strategies vary widely between hospitals. This single-center Dutch study reviewed a full decade of ANCA testing strategies at a large teaching hospital. The ten-year experience distills practical lessons for refining how and when to test.
plos-pone-0355195: Twin pregnancies carry multiplied risks for mothers and babies alike. This Brazilian nationwide population-based study examined maternal characteristics and neonatal outcomes in twin pregnancies from 2015 to 2024. The decade of population data gives obstetricians the evidence to guide safer twin care.
plos-pone-0355495: Expedited FDA pathways promise faster drug approvals — but trial complexity can clog the fast lane. This comparative analysis examined expedited pathway portfolios, trial complexity, and approval timelines in oncology and neurology. The analysis maps where the fast track actually works.
plos-pone-0356895: AI-generated content tools can now animate emotions — but personalization is the frontier. This research explored emotion animation generation using AIGC tools, with personalized expression and multi-level encoding strategies. The techniques make digital characters feel genuinely, individually expressive.
plos-pone-0356495: Healthcare workers who skip flu shots put patients at risk. This Georgian study examined the factors associated with influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers from 2021 to 2024. The findings show what actually moves hesitant health workers to roll up their sleeves.
plos-pone-0355695: Sipli sheep are a cornerstone of rural livelihoods in Punjab, Pakistan — yet their productive potential is poorly documented. This paper evaluated their morphometric traits alongside productive and reproductive performance. The comprehensive breed profile gives farmers and breeders the data to improve flocks that thousands of families depend on.
plos-pone-0356995: Planning toric lens implants for astigmatism demands precise corneal measurements — but devices disagree. This study tested the agreement of keratometry measurements from KR-800, IOLMaster 500, and Pentacam HR in routine clinical practice. The comparison tells cataract surgeons which device to trust for lens planning.
plos-pone-0356395: A 360-degree augmented-virtuality classroom promises immersive learning — but does it make students queasy or forgetful? This feasibility study measured short-term factual recall, presence, and visio-vestibular discomfort in such an environment. The results reveal the trade-offs of immersive education: stronger presence, but at what cost to comfort and memory?
plos-pone-0356295: How do middle-aged and older adults emotionally respond to everyday environmental sounds? This paper established normative responses in normal-hearing adults using stimuli from the Marcell database. The normative data provide a baseline for detecting when sound processing — and the emotions tied to it — goes awry with age or disease.
plos-pone-0355595: Hikikomori — severe social withdrawal — needs screening tools clinicians can understand and trust. This paper built interpretable machine learning for hikikomori screening: the adaptive HRI-15. The transparent 15-item tool balances predictive power with the explainability that clinical adoption demands.
plos-pone-0354895: Pregnancy after losing a baby brings haunted nights. This qualitative study explored sleep experiences in late pregnancy among women with a history of perinatal loss. Their stories reveal how grief and anxiety invade rest — and what compassionate care could offer these mothers in the dark hours.
plos-pone-0345895: Elderly hip fracture patients face deadly blood clots — and albumin levels might predict them. This retrospective study associated serum albumin with preoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients 80 and older with intertrochanteric fracture. The simple blood marker could flag who needs the most aggressive clot prevention.
plos-pone-0331995: Pyrethroid-resistant mosquitoes demand better bed nets. This paper tested MiraNet Combi — combining alpha-cypermethrin, pyriproxyfen, and piperonyl butoxide — against resistant Anopheles. The triple-action net’s efficacy data support deploying smarter nets where old ones fail.
plos-pone-0355295: Iron deficiency anemia strikes pregnant women at their first antenatal visit in Addis Ababa — at rates needing action. This paper measured its magnitude and determinants. The findings give Ethiopian maternal health programs the risk factors to target — before anemia harms mothers and babies.
europmc-pmc2800195: Using data from a large U.S. health survey, this 2010 study asks whether bisphenol A in urine tracks with heart disease. The authors analyze NHANES 2003/06 records and find higher BPA levels linked to more reported heart disease. The association does not prove cause, but it added weight to worries that this common plastic chemical affects more than hormones.
europmc-pmc2821895: Reporting guidelines help researchers write up studies clearly, but making good guidelines takes guidance itself. This 2010 paper offers advice for developers of health research reporting guidelines. Written by leaders of the EQUATOR network, it lays out best practices. The paper improved the quality of the checklists that keep medical research transparent.
europmc-pmc2857295: A fierce pig virus swept China, and this 2007 paper sounds the alarm. The authors describe the highly pathogenic porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome hitting Chinese herds. Their report flagged a new, deadlier strain. The warning spurred surveillance of a virus that threatens pork worldwide.
europmc-pmc2948795: HIV treatment only works if patients stay in care. This 2010 review tracks patient retention in African antiretroviral programs up to three years. The authors find worrying drop-off over time. Their review pushed retention onto the global agenda. Clinics now design follow-up around its lessons.
europmc-pmc2987895: The vegetative state got a kinder name. This 2010 paper proposes calling it unresponsive wakefulness syndrome instead. The authors say the new name respects patients more. Their proposal spread through brain medicine. Families found the old label cruelly cold. Journals now prefer the gentler term.
europmc-pmc3042595: Endless brooding got a clean measure. This 2011 paper tests a quiz that gauges repetitive bleak thinking. The authors show it works across disorders. Their quiz spread through clinics. Therapists track brooding scores over sessions. High scores flag relapse risk early.
europmc-pmc3048395: A gut mucus-eater got its genome read. This 2011 paper sequences Akkermansia, a germ that dines on gut mucus. The authors reveal the specialist's toolkit. Their work launched a probiotic star. Lean people carry more of the germ. Supplement makers now bottle the strain.
europmc-pmc3068995: Flu sneaks in by gulping, too. This 2011 paper shows flu virus can enter cells by gulping fluid, not just docking. The authors reveal the side door. Their work points to antivirals. Blocking the gulp stalls the infection. The route dodges some immune sensors.
europmc-pmc3098195: Tumor gene fusions got a finder. This 2011 paper brings deFuse, a program that spots fused genes in tumor RNA data. The authors' tool finds the fusions. Their software aided cancer doctors. Fusions often drive the cancer. Found fusions guide targeted drugs.
europmc-pmc6542195: New genes were long thought to arise only by copying old ones - but some are born from scratch, from stretches of DNA that never coded for anything. This review tours de novo gene birth: how non-coding DNA gains the signals to make a protein, how often it happens, and why these newborn genes matter for evolution.
europmc-pmc6554895: Proven health programs rarely survive contact with the real world unchanged - clinics adapt them, and those tweaks often go unreported. FRAME is an expanded checklist for documenting exactly what changed, why, and by whom. The framework helps researchers separate faithful delivery from smart local tailoring, so adaptations can be studied rather than hidden.
europmc-pmc6637495: Viruses do not just hijack cells - they rewire their metabolism. This review surveys how viruses reprogram host energy and building-block pathways, including cancer-causing viruses that push cells toward tumor-like metabolism. Understanding viral metabolic tricks could expose new antiviral targets.
europmc-pmc6651195: When plants face drought, salt, or cold, they brew protective phenolic compounds through the phenylpropanoid pathway. This review traces that chemical assembly line and the polyphenols' protective roles. Understanding the pathway helps breeders coax hardier crops from stressed plants.
europmc-pmc6695795: Arachidonic acid - a fat woven into cell membranes - becomes inflammation's raw material when freed. This review follows its three metabolic fates via COX, LOX, and CYP450 enzymes, and how they drive kidney inflammation. Blocking the right branch could calm the kidneys without crippling immunity.
europmc-pmc6735495: Bad childhoods cast long shadows - but good ones may cast light. While adverse experiences are tied to adult depression, this statewide study asked whether positive childhood experiences buffer mental and relational health. The answer: yes, measurably - a hopeful counterweight to the ACEs story.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1195: GAO's 2007 Iraq report card kept flunking the locals: most political, security, and economic benchmarks still unmet. The findings — issued as the surge debate raged — put official optimism on trial. The report's cold numbers asked the hottest question in Washington: was progress real, or just well-spoken?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-195: Reservists' new health benefits needed explaining in 2007, and GAO's report says the expanded TRICARE eligibility brought educational challenges. The findings target the information gaps. The report argues the part-time troops deserved full-time clarity. The citizen-soldiers earned clear answers.
openalex-w7221071495: Drug-proof staph kills, and fresh antibiotics are badly needed. This paper builds new cousins of the antibiotic cipro, spiked with nitrofuran, and tests them on resistant germs in dishes. The authors ranked their killing power. A drug-making study rearming an old pill against new defenses.
pmc-13459195: In this 2026 neuroimaging methods paper, researchers compared how body size and cardiorespiratory fitness relate to head-motion contamination in fMRI brain scans. Tiny head movements corrupt brain images, especially at high sampling rates, and the study asks whether fitness and body size predict the problem. Knowing the confounds helps researchers clean their data and trust their results.
pmc-13440595: This 2026 review tells the story of ganciclovir, a drug against human cytomegalovirus — a virus dangerous to newborns and transplant patients — from its historical development to future prospects. The paper traces how the drug was discovered, refined, and where it goes next. It is a case study in antiviral drug development.
pmc-13471995: This 2026 forensic science paper tested how different sequence-alignment tools affect the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock — a DNA-methylation-based method for estimating a person's age. In forensics, small errors matter, and the study shows tool choice isn't neutral. The findings guide standardization of age estimation.
pmc-13411295: A 2026 systematic review comparing intravenous thrombolysis plus endovascular treatment versus endovascular treatment alone for acute ischemic stroke caused by tandem lesions — blockages in two vessels. The combination question is hotly debated in stroke care. The pooled evidence guides the emergency decision.
pmc-13449895: A 2026 atmospheric science paper showing that atmospheric mixing controls air pollution chemistry and how well mitigation works in high-latitude cities. Cold, dark winters change the chemistry of smog. The findings mean pollution policy must be latitude-aware.
pmc-13389095: A 2026 radiobiology study of gold nanoparticle-enhanced radiosensitization in proton therapy — using tiny gold particles to amplify radiation damage inside tumors. Protons already spare healthy tissue; nanoparticles could make them deadlier to cancer. The study measures the enhancement in detail.
pmc-13386395: In this 2026 biophysics paper, researchers calmed amyloid-associated shape fluctuations in a protein by engineering a diselenide bridge — a selenium-based staple — into its structure. Locking the protein's conformation tames the wobbling linked to amyloid formation. The engineered bridge is a neat piece of protein design.
pmc-13481095: This 2026 case report described silicone axillary lymphadenopathy — silicone in armpit lymph nodes — after rupture of fourth-generation cohesive breast implants. Even "gummy bear" implants can fail. The case documents the complication.
pmc-13520095: In this 2026 paper, CD19xCD3 bispecific T cell engager treatment induced remission in experimental pemphigoid disease — an autoimmune blistering condition. Redirecting T cells against B cells reset the autoimmunity. The preclinical success suggests a new treatment class.
pmc-13495395: A 2026 oncology paper presenting a novel imaging-based approach for large extracellular vesicle detection and prognostic stratification in metastatic breast cancer. Vesicle imaging could guide treatment. The approach is the innovation.
pmc-13425595: A 2026 case report of ciprofloxacin-induced near-total toxic epidermal necrolysis complicated by upper GI bleeding, with ALDEN-based causality assessment. The common antibiotic caused a catastrophic reaction. The causality analysis is the method.
pmc-13599695: A 2026 randomized trial of online parent training with and without coaching support on the well-being of families of children with neurodisabilities. The coaching add-on was the experimental question. The trial measures what families gained.
pmc-13447095: A 2026 paper using single-cell spatial mapping of human kidney development to implicate the microenvironment in guiding cell fate decisions. Where a cell sits decides what it becomes. The spatial map is the resource.
pmc-13452295: A 2026 oncology paper showing ultrasensitive circulating tumor DNA detection improved prognostication in triple-negative breast cancer after neoadjuvant therapy. Finer ctDNA measurement sharpened predictions. The assay is the advance.
pmc-13530795: A 2026 conference poster reporting high functional recovery and low complications after percutaneous knotless bridge Achilles repair in athletes. The minimally invasive repair performed well. The poster presents the outcomes.
pmc-13628195: A 2026 case series and narrative review on CMV and HHV-6 reactivation in immunocompetent ICU patients — asking if it's a real problem. The viruses' ICU role was examined. The review weighs the evidence.
pmc-13501295: This 2026 oncology paper showed liquid biopsies reveal dual compartments of cancer risk from tumor and host-derived mutations. The blood test read both. The dual-compartment insight is the advance.
pmc-13573595: In this 2026 paper, PSTN — the Plant Spatio-Temporal Integration Network — provided a framework for dynamic single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in fungal-plant interactions. The framework handles space and time. The integration is the advance.
pmc-13498895: In this 2026 cancer paper, vitamin D3 and sodium selenite cooperatively suppressed ovarian cancer growth via SEPP1 induction. The nutrient combination was the therapy. The cooperation is the mechanism.
pmc-13477495: A 2026 systematic review comparing remote telesurgery versus local minimally invasive surgery — the comparative evidence base. The distance surgery's evidence was synthesized. The review is the landscape.
pmc-13448095: This 2026 mouse study examined probiotic supplementation effects on circadian rhythm-related gene expression and body weight in mice with disturbed circadian rhythms. The probiotics reset the clock genes. The effects are the finding.
pmc-13571795: A 2026 paper on diagnostic testing after positive cell-free DNA screening for sex chromosome aneuploidies — clinical and socioeconomic determinants. The follow-up testing's disparities were studied. The determinants are the finding.
pmc-13428695: A 2026 SUN cohort study finding high plant protein intake decreased all-cause mortality. The plant protein's longevity benefit was quantified. The decrease is the nutritional signal.
pmc-13388495: A 2026 pharmacology paper with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model of brigatinib in healthy volunteers and cancer patients. The lung cancer drug's disposition was modeled. The model guides dosing.
pmc-13524095: This 2026 wheat paper showed the TaMIP1 gene broke the dilemma of coordinating drought resistance and high yield. The gene delivered both. The breaking is the breeding breakthrough.
pmc-13454695: A 2026 introduction to the fundamentals of root systems research in cultivated plants. The primer covers the basics. The introduction serves students and newcomers.
pmc-13481695: A 2026 rapid evidence review assessing intervention effects on healthcare-related financial protection in low- and middle-income countries. The financial protection evidence was synthesized. The review informs policy.
pmc-13516295: A 2026 pharmacology paper on vonoprazan's effects on isolated rat lower esophageal sphincter and ileum. The acid blocker's gut effects were tested. The effects are the physiology.
pmc-13436195: This 2026 protocol described Move Together Buckinghamshire — a pragmatic mixed-methods evaluation of a community physical activity program for older adults with long-term conditions (the title is truncated). The protocol is the plan. The evaluation will test the program.
pmc-13615495: A 2026 paper targeting the peripheral nervous system in adipose tissue with engineered AAV vectors. The fat's nerves were genetically targeted. The targeting is the delivery advance.
pmc-13427795: This 2026 propensity score-matched analysis examined perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in robotic-assisted ventral hernia repair. The antibiotics' value was tested. The analysis informs surgical practice.
pmc-13527095: This 2026 chemistry paper reported catalyst-free single-molecule cascade photoreactions for spatiotemporally programmed encryption. The light-driven reactions encoded data. The encryption is the application.
pmc-13473395: A 2026 agricultural AI paper: DeepLabV3+ with MobileNetV3 backbone enhancement and multi-level fusion decoder for pepper field weed segmentation. The AI found the weeds. The segmentation serves precision farming.
pmc-13473295: A 2026 paper on vertebral body dosimetry associated with hematologic toxicities and survival in esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma treated with chemoradiotherapy plus immunotherapy (the title is truncated). The spine dose's blood effects were quantified. The dosimetry guides planning.
pmc-13439495: A 2026 trial comparing general versus spinal anesthesia effects on early postoperative cognition and 30-day daily living activities in elderly hip fracture patients (the title is truncated). The anesthesia choice's cognitive impact was tested. The comparison guides anesthesiologists.
pmc-13511295: This 2026 trial compared antimicrobial glucose chlorhexidine dressings versus sterile dressings in preventing catheter-related infections during continuous renal replacement therapy (the title is truncated). The antimicrobial dressings were tested. The comparison is the ICU evidence.
pmc-13514195: This 2026 scoping review examined emerging digital technologies for monitoring and rehabilitation support in chronic dust-induced lung diseases. The digital tools' occupational health role was mapped. The review is the evidence map.
pmc-13466695: A 2026 thyroid paper on preoperative thyroid hormone ratios and CBC-derived biomarkers for differentiating benign nodules from papillary thyroid carcinoma (the title is truncated). The blood markers distinguished the cancers. The differentiating aids surgeons.
pmc-13419195: A 2026 review: the brain as an HIV reservoir — recent findings using autopsy tissues from people with HIV. The brain's viral hiding places were mapped. The findings inform cure research.
pmc-13614295: A 2026 materials paper: vine tendril-inspired cold-programmable shape-memory polymer composites using sugar beet pulp. The plant-inspired plastics remembered shapes. The composites are the sustainable materials.
arxiv-2606-15995: Electrons carry a tiny magnetic "wobble" beyond simple theory — the anomalous magnetic dipole moment, one of the most precisely measured numbers in physics. This paper works out how that wobble shifts the behavior of heavy atoms with many protons. It is precision atomic physics, relevant to researchers testing the fundamental theories of nature.
arxiv-2606-16195: Nickel blends that carry current with zero drag are the hot new chase in physics. This paper sums, from raw math with no tuned knobs, how the charge maps shift across a kin of nickel-rock slabs spiked with rare earths. It is for solid-state hunters.
arxiv-2606-16295: Most AI assistants live on screens; this paper describes an agent built for the physical world — one that acts in real time and personalizes itself to its user. The available title is truncated, so details are limited, but the work sits at the intersection of robotics, real-time systems, and personal AI assistants.
arxiv-2606-16395: The CBM (Compressed Baryonic Matter) experiment, being built at FAIR in Germany, will smash heavy nuclei to recreate the dense matter inside neutron stars. This paper lays out the CBM physics program and recent experimental developments from the collaboration. It serves nuclear physicists following the facility's progress toward first collisions.
arxiv-2606-16695: Quirk glow can pour into spook ties — yet hiss muddies the pour. This paper charts the pour in wide halls under tame hiss maps. For quirk-stock crews who track how glow turns to tie, hiss and all. Clean pours, keen ties.
